text:
The Flyers' problem is not bad luck, or not mostly. They have 13 points from 19 games, they take 43% of the expected goals (41% at five on five), and they have blown third-period leads in back-to-back games. "Right now, this is simply a bad hockey team that finds ways to lose," Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports wrote after the overtime loss in Calgary. Our simulations give them a 2% chance at the playoffs and project about 75 points.

There is one honest bright spot, and it has become the story. Matvei Michkov has 10 points in his last 10 games, and his line with Noah Cates and Porter Martone has taken 60% of the expected goals, by far the best of any Flyers trio. Michkov has also been in the headlines all week over his ice time under Rick Tocchet, after Tocchet broke that line up for a couple of games and then put it back together. When your best line is the one the coach keeps tinkering with, that's going to be the conversation.

Some of the scoreboard is unkind: the Flyers have scored about nine fewer goals than their chances usually produce. Even with that back, though, this is a team getting outplayed most nights. What to watch is development, not the standings: how many minutes Michkov and Martone get, what Oliver Bonk and Jamie Drysdale look like on a bad team, and whether Joseph Woll keeps giving them a chance.
